sentences.text: This is an application for regular bail filed under Section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
2. Petitioner is the sole accused in Crime No.766 of 2022 of Kadavanthra Police Station, Ernakulam District.
The offences alleged against the petitioner are punishable under Sections 376(2)(n) and 506 of the Indian Penal Code,1860.

3. According to the prosecution, the accused had, after promising to marry the victim, committed rape on her at a hotel in Thiruvananthapuram in August 2022 and again repeated the said offence on various occasions, and thereafter backed out of the marriage, and threatened to publish their intimate photographs in the social media, and thereby committed the offences alleged.
4. Sri. Jai George, the learned counsel for the petitioner contended that prosecution case is false and the incident as alleged had not occurred.

It was further submitted that even if the prosecution allegations are assumed to be true, still it would only reveal instances of consensual relationship and therefore, the offence of rape will not BAIL APPL. NO. 10454 OF 2022 lie.
The learned counsel further submitted that having regard to the period of detention already undergone from 13-12-2022,
petitioner
's continued detention ought not to be allowed.
5. Sri

.Noushad K.A., the learned Public Prosecutor opposed the grant of bail and contended that the allegations are serious and that the victim is a divorcee and the petitioner had exploited her gullible position by promising to marry her and thereafter backed out of the said promise which clearly comes within the purview of the offence of rape.
6. I have considered the rival contentions and have also perused the statement of the victim and the connected records.
7. Petitioner is a married man whose divorce petition is still pending.
Petitioner is alleged to have promised to marry the victim and obtained her consent for sexual intercourse.

Even though the allegations are serious, considering the age of the petitioner as well as the victim and taking into reckoning the subsisting marriage of the petitioner, apart from the period of detention already undergone, I am of the view that further detention is not essential.

In the result, this application is allowed on the following conditions:-
(a) Petitioner shall be released on bail on him executing a bond for Rs.50,000/-
(Rupees fifty thousand only) with two solvent sureties BAIL APPL. NO. 10454 OF 2022 each for the like sum to the satisfaction of the court having jurisdiction.
(b) Petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer as and when required.
(c) Petitioner shall not intimidate or attempt to influence the witnesses; nor shall he tamper with the evidence or contact the victim or her family members.
(d) Petitioner shall not commit any similar offences while he is on bail.
